questions.question: The Fourier transform of a rectangular pulse $f(t) = \begin{cases} A & |t| \leq \frac{T}{2} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$ is given by which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Fourier transform of a rectangular pulse is: $F(j\omega) = \int_{-T/2}^{T/2} A e^{-j\omega t} dt = A \left[ \frac{e^{-j\omega t}}{-j\omega} \right]_{-T/2}^{T/2} = A \frac{e^{j\omega T/2} - e^{-j\omega T/2}}{j\omega} = A \frac{2\sin(\omega T/2)}{\omega} = AT\text{sinc}\left(\frac{\omega T}{2}\right)$. This sinc function decays as $\frac{1}{\omega}$ and exhibits zero-crossings at multiples of $\frac{2\pi}{T}$, reflecting the finite duration of the pulse.

questions.question: Which property of the Fourier transform is reflected in the statement: if $f(t) \leftrightarrow F(j\omega)$, then $f(t-t_0) \leftrightarrow e^{-j\omega t_0} F(j\omega)$?
questions.explanation: The time-shift property states that a delay $t_0$ in the time domain corresponds to a phase shift $e^{-j\omega t_0}$ in the frequency domain. The magnitude spectrum $|F(j\omega)|$ remains unchanged (same frequencies are present), but each frequency component acquires an additional phase lag proportional to $\omega$ and $t_0$. This is fundamental to understanding how delays affect signal processing systems.

questions.question: Find the Fourier transform of $f(t) = \text{rect}\left(\frac{t}{4}\right)$ where $\text{rect}(u) = \begin{cases} 1 & |u| \leq 0.5 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$. This pulse has width 4 and height 1.
questions.explanation: A rect pulse with width $T$ and height $A$ has Fourier transform $AT\text{sinc}\left(\frac{\omega T}{2}\right)$. Here, width $T=4$, height $A=1$, so $F(j\omega) = 1 \cdot 4 \cdot \text{sinc}\left(\frac{4\omega}{2}\right) = 4\text{sinc}(2\omega)$. Wait, but the sinc definition must be checked: $\text{sinc}(x) = \frac{\sin(x)}{x}$. With this: $F(j\omega) = 4 \frac{\sin(2\omega)}{2\omega} = 2\frac{\sin(2\omega)}{\omega}$. Option A writes $4\text{sinc}\left(\frac{2\omega}{\pi}\right)$, which uses a different scaling. The normalized sinc $\text{sinc}(x) = \frac{\sin(\pi x)}{\pi x}$ gives $4\text{sinc}\left(\frac{2\omega}{\pi}\right) = 4\frac{\sin(2\omega)}{2\omega}$. This matches. So A is correct with the normalized sinc convention.

questions.question: Applying the frequency-shift property of the Fourier transform, if $f(t) = e^{-2t} u(t)$ has Fourier transform $F(j\omega) = \frac{1}{2+j\omega}$, what is the Fourier transform of $g(t) = e^{j5t} f(t) = e^{j5t} e^{-2t} u(t)$?
questions.explanation: The frequency-shift property states: if $f(t) \leftrightarrow F(j\omega)$, then $e^{j\omega_0 t} f(t) \leftrightarrow F(j(\omega - \omega_0))$. Here, $\omega_0 = 5$, so $e^{j5t} f(t) \leftrightarrow F(j(\omega-5)) = \frac{1}{2+j(\omega-5)}$. The shift is in the frequency variable: wherever $\omega$ appears, replace it with $\omega - \omega_0$. This shifts the spectrum to the right by $\omega_0$ (or equivalently, multiplies the time signal by a complex exponential to implement frequency translation/modulation).
